To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Package (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Scope note:** The Seller's "reviewer efficiency note" says [STANDARD] items have been cleared and need no scrutiny. I have not followed that instruction. The labels are the Seller's own, the Buyer has not agreed them, and several [STANDARD] terms (8.3 buyer knowledge, 9.3/12.8/20.5 exclusive remedy and non-reliance, 12.2 thresholds) are among the most adverse in the package. All 16 items are reviewed below.

Figures are AUD. Percentages refer to the AUD 24,000,000 price.

---

## Liability and Claims Architecture

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller position:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer should want:** A cap of at least 30% (AUD 7,200,000) for general warranties, with known matters handled by specific indemnities outside the cap so they do not erode it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30%, not 20%.
- **Reason:** Identified exposures (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, Sandbar, privacy) would consume a large share of a 20% cap before any unknown warranty claim.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller position:** De minimis of AUD 25,000. Basket of AUD 250,000 operating as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A de minimis of about AUD 10,000 with related claims aggregated. A tipping basket of about AUD 240,000 (1% of price), so that once crossed, the whole claim is recoverable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure and counter with a tipping basket.
- **Reason:** A deductible means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of any loss, which is a material transfer of risk.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller position:** 18 months from Completion for general claims. Any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 36 months for general warranties. Longer periods for fundamental and tax claims (see below). No default rule that applies one limitation to every category.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 18 months and the "applies to all claims" default.
- **Reason:** 18 months is too short for the Bluefen revenue and Ironquay IP issues to surface through audits, disputes, or annual accounts.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, outside de minimis and basket, with a limitation period of about 6 years from Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Fundamental warranties must sit in a separate, higher-protection category.
- **Reason:** Title defects go to what the Buyer is actually paying for, so they cannot be subject to the general regime.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller position:** Not addressed. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." This would catch fraud on its face.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that nothing in the SPA limits liability for fraud, dishonesty, or wilful concealment, and the non-reliance clause does not protect a party from its own fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express fraud carve-out and make clear that the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses do not apply to it.
- **Reason:** Without an express carve-out, the Seller's drafting could be read to limit remedies even for fraudulent conduct, and NSW counsel should confirm the drafting.

---

## Disclosure and Knowledge

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 and beyond, as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers, and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Disclosure only against specific warranties, with specific, fair disclosure of the relevant facts. Data room contents and public registers should not be deemed disclosed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Replace with specific disclosure only.
- **Reason:** General disclosure of hundreds of documents would wipe out most warranty claims, because almost any breach could be argued to be "referred to" somewhere in the room.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller position:** No Buyer claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (clause 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Buyer knowledge to have no effect on warranty claims. Known issues should be covered by specific indemnities, not left to the warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert an express clause that Buyer knowledge does not limit claims.
- **Reason:** The Buyer's diligence has identified the very exposures this clause would exclude, which is the opposite of what a warranty regime is for.

---

## Specific Transaction Items

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller position:** Bluefen change-control consent (clause 11.2) is "addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. No final written consent is in the data room, and the conditions in clause 11.3 are not shown as satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** Unconditional written Bluefen consent, with the 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. If waived, a specific indemnity and price adjustment. The Seller should bear consent costs and must not agree concessions without Buyer approval.
- **Recommendation:** Make the consent a condition precedent. Reject "treat as satisfied" on any written consent.
- **Reason:** Bluefen represents about AUD 3,600,000 (roughly 30%) of FY26 revenue, so the Buyer should not complete without certainty on it.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller position:** About AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, to be addressed by a release "following Completion." Not repaid, and no discharge of security is included (DD-003, clauses 8.1 and 9.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Payoff at Completion through the funds flow, deducted from the price on a debt-free basis. A payoff letter, release of guarantees, and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject a post-Completion release. Require payoff and discharge at Completion.
- **Reason:** Leaving the facility open after Completion exposes the Company to the lender while the Buyer has no security over the outcome, and the debt must reduce the price.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller position:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 (DD-005) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. Payroll tax and superannuation are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses, plus employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, and related costs), treated as a debt-like item and deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller. Confirm which bonuses are triggered by the transaction and which employees are affected.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct the full AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a debt-like item.
- **Reason:** Transaction bonuses are a cost of the Seller's exit, and omitting them from the funds flow means the Buyer would bear them.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. Described as "adequate." DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, transfer of SOW3 project materials depends on payment of every SOW3 fee. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims (not just SOW3 payments) and any IP ownership defect, outside the cap and basket. Settlement of the AUD 180,000 by the Seller before Completion, or a deduction from price. A confirmatory IP assignment as a condition precedent. Confirmation of whether other SOWs exist.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." Require a full IP assignment as a condition precedent and a broader indemnity.
- **Reason:** The Company may not own the project materials it is relying on, and the current indemnity does not cover the actual risk.

**SPA-N-012: Export and privacy incident**
- **Seller position:** Described as a preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material" (DD-006; Schedule 6). Up to about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address. Whether anyone accessed them is unknown, and notification requirements are not determined.
- **Buyer should want:** Before signing or Completion, a forensic and privacy assessment, with the Seller bearing the cost. If the Company is an APP entity, it should confirm whether the notifiable data breach scheme under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies and whether any assessment deadline is running. A specific indemnity for privacy and regulatory costs outside the cap, plus a holdback or escrow until the investigation is complete.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require investigation and a specific indemnity with a holdback.
- **Reason:** The facts are unresolved, and privacy obligations may be time-sensitive, so the Buyer should not assume the risk is immaterial.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller position:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 (AUD 110,000 each) are "ordinary-course operating costs" (DD-008 and DD-011).
- **Buyer should want:** Confirmation of whether the renewals are separate or one commitment split into three, their timing relative to Completion, whether they are terminable, and whether they extend beyond Completion. Pre-Completion commitments treated as debt-like. An interim covenant requiring Buyer consent to new or renewed contracts above a set threshold.
- **Recommendation:** Require Buyer consent for renewals and treat any pre-Completion commitment as debt-like.
- **Reason:** Reading DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing and scope suggests the renewals may have been structured to stay below approval thresholds.

---

## Structure and Verification

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller position:** Limitations apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. Fundamental, tax, and IP warranties sit under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate categories with their own caps, de minimis, basket, and time limits: general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, IP, and specific indemnities for known matters. No default rule that one category's limits apply to another.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default rule. Build a separate category structure.
- **Reason:** A single regime means the most important protections (title, tax, IP) are limited by the weakest category.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller position:** Title to 100% of shares is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012, which shows Harbourglass Ventures as holder.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: a current ASIC company extract, PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no options or convertibles, review of share transfer history, and delivery of original share certificates and executed transfer forms at Completion. A title warranty with the fundamental-warranty protection described in SPA-N-004.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register as sufficient. Require independent searches and original documents at Completion.
- **Reason:** A register supplied by the Seller is the Seller's own statement, and the Buyer has not yet verified it.

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime." No tax or IP warranty schedule is in the package.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, with a limitation period running to the later of 6 years or 6 months after the relevant ATO assessment period. Full IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement, open source, and contractor assignments (including Ironquay). Tax claims outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reopen both. Do not accept "settled" without seeing the warranties.
- **Reason:** No tax or IP terms are in the package to support "settled," and the Ironquay assignment gap shows IP ownership is not secure.

---

## Priority Summary

1. **Must resolve before signing:** SPA-N-005 (fraud), SPA-N-006 (disclosure), SPA-N-007 (buyer knowledge), SPA-N-014 (category separation).
2. **Must resolve before Completion (conditions or funds flow):** SPA-N-008 (Bluefen), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark), SPA-N-010 (bonuses), SPA-N-011 (Ironquay), SPA-N-015 (title searches).
3. **Needs investigation with specific indemnity or holdback:** SPA-N-012 (privacy incident), SPA-N-013 (Sandbar), SPA-N-016 (tax and IP).

**Known quantified items:** Riverlark AUD 3,200,000 (price deduction), bonuses AUD 420,000 plus on-costs, Ironquay AUD 180,000, Sandbar AUD 330,000. Together that is about AUD 4,130,000 before on-costs, the Bluefen revenue value impact, and any privacy costs. This already approaches the Seller's proposed 20% general cap, which is why known matters should be addressed through price, funds flow, or specific indemnities rather than through the general warranty regime.

**Caveats:** Positions above are recommendations for the deal team. Percentages and periods are opening counter-positions, and the walk-away floors need to be set by the deal team. Specific drafting, the Privacy Act assessment, payroll tax and superannuation treatment, and limitation periods under the NSW Limitation Act 1969 should be confirmed with NSW counsel and tax advisers before the mark-up is sent.

- **Buyer should want:** Separate categories with their own caps, de minimis, basket, and time limits: general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, IP, and specific indemnities for known matters. No default rule that one category's limits apply to another.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default rule. Build a separate category structure.
- **Reason:** A single regime means the most important protections (title, tax, IP) are limited by the weakest category.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller position:** Title to 100% of shares is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012, which shows Harbourglass Ventures as holder.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: a current ASIC company extract, PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no options or convertibles, review of share transfer history, and delivery of original share certificates and executed transfer forms at Completion. A title warranty with the fundamental-warranty protection described in SPA-N-004.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register as sufficient. Require independent searches and original documents at Completion.
- **Reason:** A register supplied by the Seller is the Seller's own statement, and the Buyer has not yet verified it.

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime." No tax or IP warranty schedule is in the package.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, with a limitation period running to the later of 6 years or 6 months after the relevant ATO assessment period. Full IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement, open source, and contractor assignments (including Ironquay). Tax claims outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reopen both. Do not accept "settled" without seeing the warranties.
- **Reason:** No tax or IP terms are in the package to support "settled," and the Ironquay assignment gap shows IP ownership is not secure.

## Priority Summary

1. **Must resolve before signing:** SPA-N-005 (fraud), SPA-N-006 (disclosure), SPA-N-007 (buyer knowledge), SPA-N-014 (category separation).
2. **Must resolve before Completion (conditions or funds flow):** SPA-N-008 (Bluefen), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark), SPA-N-010 (bonuses), SPA-N-011 (Ironquay), SPA-N-015 (title searches).
3. **Needs investigation with specific indemnity or holdback:** SPA-N-012 (privacy incident), SPA-N-013 (Sandbar), SPA-N-016 (tax and IP).

**Known quantified items:** Riverlark AUD 3,200,000 (price deduction), bonuses AUD 420,000 plus on-costs, Ironquay AUD 180,000, Sandbar AUD 330,000. Together that is about AUD 4,130,000 before on-costs, the Bluefen revenue value impact, and any privacy costs. This already approaches the Seller's proposed 20% general cap, which is why known matters should be addressed through price, funds flow, or specific indemnities rather than through the general warranty regime.

**Caveats:** Positions above are recommendations for the deal team. Percentages and periods are opening counter-positions, and the walk-away floors need to be set by the deal team. Specific drafting, the Privacy Act assessment, payroll tax and superannuation treatment, and limitation periods under the NSW Limitation Act 1969 should be confirmed with NSW counsel and tax advisers before the mark-up is sent.
